I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the cropping pattern that fits my land, water, labor, and weather best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the most reliable way for me to use the full year on the North China Plain. At my age, I care more about steady output and manageable fieldwork than chasing risky changes. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because they give me better stand, better yield stability, and they are already familiar to me. I will prepare the wheat field with rotary tillage after the maize season residue is handled, then manage the maize with lighter tillage after wheat harvest so I can sow quickly and keep moisture. I will apply moderate fertilizer, with more nitrogen on maize because it responds strongly, and balanced phosphorus and potassium to keep the soil from running down. I will irrigate wheat more times because it depends on key water stages like overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling, while maize will get fewer irrigations unless rainfall is poor. I will spray only as much as needed to control weeds, aphids, rust, corn borer, and leaf diseases, because too many applications waste money. My goal is stable grain yield, simple management, and lower risk.
